summary.p1: Cogar is an independent social networking platform built around the Irish language, designed to make using Irish online a normal, everyday experience.
summary.p2: Conceived as a personal project, Cogar has grown into a fully functioning social platform with over 5,100 registered users, available on both iOS and Android.
summary.p3: As the founder and sole developer, I have taken Cogar from initial concept through product design, engineering, deployment and ongoing operation. I am responsible for the entire technical lifecycle, including product architecture, UX/UI design, mobile and backend development, infrastructure, security, moderation systems, analytics and maintenance.
summary.p4: I also founded and independently manage Cogar Teicneolaíochta Ltd, the Irish company behind the platform. This extends my responsibilities beyond engineering into business strategy, commercial development, advertising, partnerships, regulatory compliance and day-to-day company operations.
summary.p5: Built primarily with React Native, Expo, TypeScript, Supabase and Cloudflare, Cogar incorporates social feeds, user and organisation profiles, private messaging, groups, events, notifications, media, content moderation and an integrated advertising platform.
summary.p6: Cogar is a practical case study in end-to-end product ownership and founder-led engineering. It demonstrates my ability to conceive and architect a complex product, make technical and commercial decisions, deliver production-ready software, and independently operate and evolve a live platform serving thousands of users.

consultancy.title: Technical Consulting / System Design
consultancy.description: A clear, honest look at your app, codebase and delivery.

summary.p1: With over 16 years of experience in software engineering and technical leadership, I bring an extensive background in hands-on development, system architecture, systems integration, orchestration and automation.
summary.p2: My work spans everything from designing and building individual applications to architecting complex, interconnected platforms, modernising legacy systems and developing scalable technical infrastructure. I combine practical engineering experience with a broader understanding of product development, business requirements and long-term technical strategy.
summary.p3: Over the years, I've worked with organisations including Web Summit, The Next Web (TNW), Run Republic and UnitOpsMedia, contributing to the design, development and operation of digital products, publishing platforms, internal tooling and business-critical systems.
summary.p4: My approach is grounded in hands-on engineering, with a particular focus on pragmatic system design, API integrations, workflow orchestration, automation and AI-assisted development. I'm equally comfortable working at an architectural level, evaluating technologies and designing systems, or getting directly involved in implementation.
summary.p5: I focus on building technology that solves real problems, reduces operational complexity and remains practical to maintain and evolve as requirements change.

engineering.title: Mobile, Web & Product Engineering
engineering.description: Senior mobile, web and full-stack engineering, with modern tooling.

summary.p1: I'm an experienced senior developer with over 16 years of building software, including time as CTO of The Next Web (TNW). My work has ranged from early web platforms to iOS and Android apps used by thousands of people every day. Today my focus is React Native and Expo, backed by TypeScript, modern backends and a full-stack understanding of how all the pieces fit together.
summary.p2: I build apps the way modern products need to be built: typed end to end, component-driven, tested and shipped through automated pipelines. That means Expo Router and EAS for builds and over-the-air updates, Reanimated for fluid, native-feeling interaction, and well-structured state and data layers that stay fast as the product grows.
summary.p3: Behind the app, I'm comfortable owning the rest of the stack: APIs and integrations, Supabase and Postgres, edge infrastructure on Cloudflare, CI/CD, monitoring and release management for the App Store and Google Play.
summary.p4: I use AI coding tools where they genuinely help, such as scaffolding, refactoring, tests and documentation, and leave them out where they don't. Everything they produce gets reviewed and owned like any other code, because the judgement about what to ship still matters most.
summary.p5: Where it suits the product, I can also build AI features properly: LLM integrations, search over your own documents and data, and automations that connect to the tools your team already uses.
summary.p6: Whether I'm joining an existing team, leading a mobile build or taking a product from idea to the stores, the goal is the same: well-engineered software that ships, performs and is a pleasure to use.

privacy.lead: What we collect, why, and what you can do about it. Short version: only what you send us, only to reply to you.

who.title: Who we are
who.p1: Busy Little Pixels is a sole proprietorship run by Rónán Ó Laoire, registered in Amsterdam, the Netherlands (KVK {kvk}). We are the controller of the personal data described in this policy.
who.p2: Questions about your data can be sent to <email>{address}</email>.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.form: Contact form. When you send a message we receive your name, email address and the content of your message.
collect.cookies: Cookies. We set a single cookie to remember whether you accepted or declined our cookie notice. It stores no personal information and expires after 12 months. We do not use analytics, advertising or tracking cookies.
collect.technical: Technical data. Like any website, our hosting provider may briefly log technical information such as your IP address and browser type to keep the site secure and running.

why.title: Why we use it
why.p1: We use the details you send through the contact form only to read and reply to your enquiry and, if we end up working together, to prepare a proposal or agreement. The legal basis is your consent, given when you tick the box on the form, and our legitimate interest in responding to business enquiries. We never sell your data or use it for marketing without asking.

share.title: Who we share it with
share.p1: Contact form messages are delivered to our inbox by Resend, an email delivery service that processes the message on our behalf. Resend may process data outside the European Economic Area; where it does, the transfer is covered by appropriate safeguards such as the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses. We do not share your data with anyone else unless the law requires it.

retention.title: How long we keep it
retention.p1: We keep enquiries for as long as needed to respond and follow up, and delete them within two years if no working relationship follows. If we do work together, related correspondence is kept for as long as Dutch tax and accounting law requires (currently seven years).

rights.title: Your rights
rights.p1: Under the GDPR you can ask us to access, correct, delete or export your personal data, object to or restrict how we use it, and withdraw your consent at any time. Withdrawing consent does not affect anything we did with your data before you withdrew it.
rights.p2: To make a request, email <email>{address}</email>. If you are unhappy with how we handle your data, you can complain to the Dutch data protection authority, the <ap>Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens</ap>.
